title: How do we mark parallel and perpendicular lines in a drawing?
description: A drawing has two flat parallel lines, two slanting parallel lines and an upright line crossing a flat line. The board marks the first set with one arrow, the second set with two arrows, and the right angle with a small square. Keeko doubts that ninety must be written in the corner.
teaching_notes: One idea: arrow marks show sets of parallel lines, one arrow for the first set and two for the second, and a small square shows a right angle. Watch for students who write the number in the corner instead of the square.

source: A drawing has two flat parallel lines, two slanting parallel lines, and one upright line that crosses a flat line at 90°. How are these marked?
video_script.why: The child learns the marks mathematicians use for parallel and perpendicular lines.
video_script.substitution: The book's own notation: an arrow mark for a set of parallel lines, two arrow marks for the second set, and a square between perpendicular lines.
video_script.anchor: A drawing of two flat lines, two slanting lines, and one upright line crossing a flat line.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the right angle must be marked with its number.
video_script.payoff_line: One arrow on each flat line, two on each slanting line, and a square at the corner.

final_answer.value: One arrow on each flat line, two arrows on each slanting line, and a square at the right angle
final_answer.spoken: one arrow on each flat line, two arrows on each slanting line, and a square at the right angle

hold_back: One arrow on each flat line, two arrows on each slanting line, and a square at the right angle
maths_rules: the first set of parallel lines, the flat lines, gets one arrow mark on each
the second set of parallel lines, the slanting lines, gets two arrow marks on each
the upright line and the flat line are perpendicular, so a small square is drawn in the corner between them
the square already says the angle is 90, so the number is not written
the slip: writing 90 in the corner instead of the square
video_script.design: One drawing stays on the stage. The marks arrive one set at a time: one arrow on the flat lines, two arrows on the slanting lines, and a small square at the corner.
